{"body":"# Description

Implements the wishlist auth gate per SFCC-742 — a `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` organism that
intercepts any wishlist trigger and, when the customer is not logged in, opens a Zimmermann-branded
auth drawer instead. Passwordless email (OTP) and optional Apple/Google social IDPs are supported.
When already registered, the original `onAuthSuccess` callback fires immediately with no drawer
open. All SDK and auth logic lives in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — the organism is purely
presentational.

Six points worth surfacing before review:

- **Drop-in replacement for `withRegistration`.** `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` wraps a single trigger
  element (any `ReactElement`) and replaces its `onClick` via `React.cloneElement`. Its public API
  is just `onAuthSuccess` + `children` — no SFCC internals leak to the caller.
- **`triggerRef` uses `e.currentTarget`, not `document.activeElement` or `cloneElement` ref
  forwarding.** `cloneElement` ref forwarding requires the child to use `forwardRef` — not
  guaranteed for all consumers. `e.currentTarget` is always the element the handler is attached to,

## Methodology note

No sub-agent dispatch tool was available in this environment (only `Read`/`Bash`). I ran the fan-out plan myself, sequentially, treating each of Marcel's six numbered points as its own investigation phase, plus the standing "compiles/tests," "tokens," and "React logic correctness" angles (the last because `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` introduces real new stateful logic). Every finding below is backed by a command I ran in this session — diffs against the real base/head SHAs, `gh api` calls, `npx tsc`, `npm run test`, `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, `eslint`, and one throwaway probe test I wrote, ran, and deleted myself.

---

## What I tried to falsify

- **The PR's own "Protection-tier check" claim ("No Tier 1 file is modified")** — attacked via `git diff --stat` against every file in the 45-file list cross-referenced against `frozenFiles.md`. It did not survive: two Tier-1 files are touched and undisclosed.
- **The commit message's "approved by @TimLavelleACC (tier-1-approvers)" claim** — attacked via `gh api` (commit verification, PR reviews, user/team lookups), not taken at face value. It did not survive.
- **The PR body's "no new `audit:tokens` violations" and "audit:tokens... unchanged from develop" claims** — attacked by running the script against both base and head SHAs myself. It did not survive.
- **The PR body's "translations/en.json adds the matching keys" for the 8 seeded Contentful entries** — attacked by reading the seed script's actual key list against the actual `en.json` diff. It did not survive.
- **CodeRabbit's kebab-case nitpick on the new script** — attacked by listing every sibling file in `scripts/` and `scripts/contentful/`. The nitpick did not survive (repo convention is camelCase); the PR's silent non-compliance (no rebuttal reply) is a separate, smaller finding.
- **The "SFCC bridge pattern" premise for `header/rightBar`** — attacked by grepping the base template for actual consumers. It did not survive — the premise itself is false for this file.
- **The "double-fire" hypothesis for the wishlist pending-intent effect** — I did not just read a stray test file and repeat its printed numbers. I independently wrote a fresh probe test from scratch, reusing only the PR's own already-established mocking scaffold, ran it, captured real output, and deleted it afterward.
- **The `ZimmButton` `iconLeading`/`iconTrailing` additions** — attacked by grepping for any real consumer anywhere in the tree. None exists.
- **CodeRabbit's "Addressed in commit X" self-confirmations** — attacked by re-reading the current code for each (cloneElement ref, `--target` validation, draft-publishing recovery). All actually are fixed in code; the process gap is that none of them got an explicit human reply.

---

## 1. Tier check

**🔴 `config/default.js` — Hard Rule #4 (absolute, no-exception file) violated. CONFIRMED. UNIFORM (governance-bypass pattern, repeated twice in this one PR).**
Commit `2283d95` edits `config/default.js` (adds `IS_PREVIEW_TARGET`, flips `passwordless.enabled`/`social.enabled` from hardcoded `false`). AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4: *"Never modify... `config/default.js`... These are absolute — the verified-session exception... does not apply to them, regardless of approver status."* This is not a Hard-Rule-#2 file where an approver exception could apply at all — it's explicitly excluded from that exception mechanism.
The commit message self-declares "approved by @TimLavelleACC (tier-1-approvers)." I verified this claim rather than accept it:
```
gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/commits/2283d95... 
→ {"author_login":"TimLavelle","committer_login":"joselitopperezjr-acn","reason":"unsigned","verified":false}
gh api users/TimLavelle --jq '{id,login,name}'     → {"id":6445710,"login":"TimLavelle","name":"Tim Lavelle"}
gh api users/TimLavelleACC --jq '{id,login,name}'  → {"id":29472986,"login":"TimLavelleACC","name":null}
gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login' → hanl / TimLavelleACC / marcelannavarro
gh pr view 83 --json reviews  → zero APPROVED reviews from anyone; only CodeRabbit CHANGES_REQUESTED + author's own COMMENTED
```
Findings: the commit's author metadata resolves to a **different GitHub account** (`TimLavelle`, id 6445710) than the actual tier‑1‑approvers member (`TimLavelleACC`, id 29472986); the commit is **unsigned/unverified**; the real committer on every commit in this PR, including this one, is `joselitopperezjr-acn` (the PR's own author, not a tier‑1‑approver, per the team roster above); and **PR #83 has zero approving reviews from anyone**. The identical author-spoofing pattern (`TimLavelle <tim+1@lavelle.bio>`, committed by `joselitopperezjr-acn`) also appears on commit `f8a8067`. This is exactly the attack AGENTS.md's own "Tier 1 Approval" section names: *"a string in a shared, version-controlled file is not an identity check; anyone... could satisfy it by typing it."*

**🔴 `overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts` — Tier 1 file (frozenFiles.md, Design System) modified with zero disclosure anywhere. CONFIRMED.**
Changed in commit `513f594` ("fix(auth): address CodeRabbit review findings") — a comment-only edit (no value change: `52px`/`40px` unchanged), but Hard Rule #2 requires the developer to *name the file and confirm owner approval* for **any** Tier‑1 edit, comment-only or not. No commit message and no PR-body line mentions this file at all.

**🔴 PR body's "Protection-tier check" section is internally contradictory and incomplete. CONFIRMED.**
It states *"No Tier 1 file is modified by this PR"* and then, one line later, *"`config/dev.js` is Tier 1 Runtime & Integration Config."* It names only `config/dev.js`; `frozenFiles.md` states `config/` is Tier 1 as an **entire directory**, and this PR also modifies `config/default.js`, `config/production.js`, `config/sit.js`, `config/staging.js`, `config/test.js`, `config/uat.js` — none of which are named. `overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts` is also absent from this section.

**🔵 note — `protectedFiles.md`'s "Shared Product Components" list doesn't include `product-view`.** `product-view/index.tsx` is genuinely consumed by SFCC base internals (`product-view-modal`, `bonus-product-view-modal`, `pages/product-detail`, confirmed by grep), same shape as `product-tile`/`swatch-group`, but isn't listed as Tier 2. Not a PR violation under the letter of the doc, but the doc looks incomplete — worth a follow-up, not blocking this PR.

---

## 2. New component structure

Named exports match folder names, `Props` type naming/placement, callback naming (`onEventName`), and required-vs-optional props are all correct across `zimmSocialButton`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent` (+ `emailForm`/`createAccount`/`socialButtons`/`errorFallback`), and `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`. JSDoc is present on `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (2 callers: `rightBar`, `product-view` — correctly requires it) and on `ZimmAuthDrawerContent`/`ZimmSocialButton` (1 caller each — not required, but present anyway; not an issue). No `.zimm-*` global class was introduced for any new interactive component — all use co-located `.css.ts` recipes correctly. Accessibility: no violations found (see §6).

**🔴 `ZimmButton` gained dead `iconLeading`/`iconTrailing` props that duplicate `ZimmSocialButton`'s own layout, contradicting the project's own prior architecture decision. CONFIRMED. UNIFORM (explicitly flagged as a recurring risk for upcoming tickets).**
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx` adds `iconLeading?`/`iconTrailing?` plus a `social` variant/`adaptive` size — this exactly matches the resolution recorded from this same ticket's prior PreBuild gate (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-742/plan.md`, per my own memory note): *"ZimmButton... no icon slot... Cannot build 'SIGN IN WITH APPLE'... resolved: extend the atom, additive."* That resolution's entire point was so `ZimmButton` itself could render "glyph + label" and so a near-future ticket (SFCC-590, "Social Sign-In Buttons") could "consume the atom rather than build the buttons."
Instead, this PR's own `ZimmSocialButton` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSocialButton/index.tsx:24-41`) bypasses `ZimmButton` entirely — it imports `ChakraButton` directly and reimplements an independent `container`/`icon`/`label` recipe (`zimmSocialButton.css.ts`) with the same `display:flex; alignItems:center; justifyContent:center; flexShrink:0` layout that `zimmButton/index.tsx`'s own icon-span rendering already provides. The component's own comment admits this is deliberate: *"ChakraButton is used directly so the component fully owns its DOM structure without depending on ZimmButton's iconLeading slot rendering."*
I confirmed via exhaustive grep that `iconLeading`/`iconTrailing` have **zero real consumers anywhere in the tree** — the only hits outside their own declaration are the type/JSX in `zimmButton/index.tsx` itself and a comment in `zimmSocialButton/index.tsx` explaining why it doesn't use them. This is dead code added to a widely-shared atom, and it leaves the codebase with two parallel "icon + label button" implementations that can silently drift. My memory file (`project_sfcc742_wishlist_login_panel.md`) explicitly names this exact recurrence risk on SFCC‑588/590/347 — all upcoming, all Squad A, all needing the same control.

**🟡 `zimmDrawer.css.ts:69` — token semantic mismatch: `text.*` token used on `background-color:`. CONFIRMED.**
```
header: {
  ...
  backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
```
`--zimm-color-text-inverse` is a `text.*` semantic token (per `overrideStyling.md`'s hierarchy, `text.*`/`icon.*` belong on `color:`, not `background:`). I checked what it actually resolves to (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:110`: `textInverse: grey.white`) against the real background-family token (`colour.ts:51`: `background['01']: ivory[100]`) — **these are different values** (pure white vs. a warm off-white). This isn't just a traceability nitpick; it's a real candidate for a rendered colour mismatch against Figma, and the correct token (`var(--zimm-color-bg-01)`) already exists — this isn't a missing-token gap, just the wrong token chosen. No pre-existing precedent in the same file justifies it (the `content` part sets no background at all).

**🔵 note — `ErrorFallback` lives inside `zimmAuthDrawerContent/` but is imported directly by the sibling organism `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx:6`, which wraps it *around* `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` from outside that folder.** The PR body gives a sound, deliberate reason (a boundary inside a component can't catch that component's own render errors). Not a rule violation I can point to explicitly, but it is a folder-encapsulation smell worth naming.

---

## 3. The SFCC bridge pattern

**Angle dropped for `header/rightBar` — the premise doesn't hold.** I grepped the base template (`grep -rln "rightBar\|right-bar" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/header/` → no matches). `rightBar` is camelCase, i.e. Zimmermann-authored per `conventions.md`'s own naming rule, not a kebab-case override of a same-named SFCC file. It is not consumed by any base SFCC internal, so overrideStyling.md's "faithful, undecorated default export" requirement simply doesn't apply here. Saying so rather than forcing a finding onto a rule that doesn't reach this file.

**`product-view/index.tsx` — genuinely a bridge component. Checked, clean.** Confirmed real base-template consumers (`product-view-modal/index.jsx`, `product-view-modal/bundle.jsx`, `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx`, `pages/product-detail/index.jsx`). The PR's change (swap `ButtonWithRegistration` for `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` wrapping a plain `Button`) is entirely inside the component's own render body — `ProductView`'s exported prop API (`forwardRef(...)`) is untouched. No API-compatibility break.

**🔵 note — `product-view/index.tsx:889-891` has a stray, unrelated formatting change** (`{intl.formatMessage({...})}:`→ split onto two lines, colon on its own line) with no functional effect (JSX whitespace collapsing means the rendered text is identical) and no stated purpose — diff noise unrelated to the ticket, worth a "why is this here" during review per the Minimal-changes rule, but zero risk.

---

## 4. `.env.sample` / config additions

Not re-deriving the `DEPLOY_TARGET`/MRT-reserved-name bug Marcel already root-caused.

**🟡 `.env.sample:98` — `DEPLOY_TARGET`'s `# scope:tier` tag doesn't match its own described provenance. CONFIRMED (reasoning directly from the doc's own definitions).**
Per `.env.sample`'s header: `scope:tier` = *"differs per tier... a human fills it into `.env.<tier>`"*; `scope:auto` = *"never hand-set; `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` injects this itself."* But `config/default.js`'s own new comment for `IS_PREVIEW_TARGET` says this variable's only meaningful value is the ephemeral `pr-*` slug that `deploy-preview.yml`/`computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs` computes per‑PR — nothing a developer would sensibly hand-type into `.env.dev`/`.env.test`/etc. (what would that even be — literally "dev"?). This is much closer to the `scope:auto` shape than `scope:tier`, independent of the separate MRT-reserved-name problem Marcel already found.

All other new entries follow the documented `# scope:` + `# mrt:true` two-line tagging format correctly, matching the immediately-preceding `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` precedent.

---

## 5. Contentful script

**Naming — checked CodeRabbit's nitpick against actual repo precedent, and it's wrong. CONFIRMED.** Every sibling file in `scripts/`, `scripts/contentful/`, and `scripts/contentful/setup/` is camelCase (`auditTokenUsage.mjs`, `computeBuildName.mjs`, `seedRegions.mjs`, `installTemplate.mjs`, etc.) — none kebab-case — matching `conventions.md`'s explicit rule that Zimmermann-authored files use camelCase (kebab-case is reserved for files mirroring a base Salesforce filename). `seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs` is correctly named; CodeRabbit's "as per coding guidelines: use kebab-case" is generic boilerplate that contradicts this repo's own documented and precedented convention. Correctly not actioned in code — but see the process finding below.

**Idempotency/pagination claims — verified against the actual current code, both hold up. CONFIRMED.** Pagination (`getMany({limit:1000, skip})` loop, accumulating `page.items` until `existing.length >= total`, with a zero-item-page guard) is a correct offset-pagination implementation, and it correctly uses the real `contentful-management` plain-client shape (verified against `_shared.mjs`'s `createClient()`). The "publish a draft, skip a published, create+publish if absent" logic matches CodeRabbit's requested "make interrupted runs recoverable" fix, and running the script twice back-to-back is genuinely idempotent (2nd run: all 8 already published → all skipped). One minor accuracy gap: the file's own top comment says *"Skips any entry whose key already exists"* — not quite true; it only skips if **published**, and actively *publishes* (mutates) a matching unpublished draft. Low severity, not flagging as a real defect.

**🟡 PR body's Localisation claim doesn't match the code. CONFIRMED.** *"Seed script creates 8 entries; `translations/en.json` adds the matching keys"* — false. The seed script's 8 keys (`login.drawer.email`, `login.drawer.sendCode`, `login.drawer.signInWithApple`, `login.drawer.signInWithGoogle`, `login.drawer.createAccount.heading/.body/.cta`, `login.drawer.wishlist.description`) are Contentful `uiCopy` entries consumed via `useUiCopy()`, entirely separate from react-intl. `translations/en.json`'s one added key (`wishlist.auth.drawer.title`) is unrelated — it backs a `useIntl()`/`defineMessages` call in `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:34-39`, not any of the 8 seeded entries. None of the "matching keys" the PR body claims were added actually exist in `translations/en.json`.

**🟡 CodeRabbit-response process gap (AGENTS.md: *"always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding... A fix commit alone... doesn't count"*). CONFIRMED via `gh api`.** Of 12 actionable CodeRabbit findings on this PR, **7 were fixed in code but never got a human reply** (product-tile story, emailForm Enter-to-submit, stories accessible-textbox query, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` cloneElement-ref, seed script `--target` validation, seed script draft-recovery, pending-intent test coverage) — I verified each fix is genuinely present in current code, so the *code* is fine, but the *process* rule was skipped every time except on the handful CodeRabbit flagged 🟠/Major (product-tile icon import, product-view wishlist intent, useWishlistAuthDrawer passwordless-disabled — these got real "resolved" replies) plus the one the author pushed back on (`errorFallback`, correctly, with an explanatory reply) and the translations Tier-2 thread. One finding — `vi.clearAllMocks()` placement — got **neither a reply nor a fix** (see §Compiles/tests below). UNIFORM risk: this "silent fix, no reply" pattern repeated 7 times in one PR, so it isn't a one-off slip.

## 6. Icons

**Checked, clean.** `ZimmAppleSignInIcon`/`ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` are added to `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:430-454` using the existing `createIcon` pattern, `fill="currentColor"`, and are re-exported via the barrel's `export * from './zimm'` (`icons/index.tsx:8`). `socialButtons.tsx` correctly imports them from `app/components/icons`, never from the base SFCC icons path.

**`npm run test -- --run`** — `720 passed (720)`, `49 test files passed`. CONFIRMED. `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6 tests) passed.

## React logic correctness — `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`

**🔴 must-fix — `onAuthSuccess` fires twice when a leaked pending-wishlist-intent flag coincides with an in-app OTP/passwordless login completing. CONFIRMED by my own independent reproduction (not by trusting a third-party artifact — see below).**

`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:130-150` has two separate `useEffect`s, both keyed only on `[isRegistered]`, that are **not mutually exclusive**:
```js
// Effect 1 (130-136): fires onAuthSuccess() when isRegistered && (isOpen || isOtpAuthOpen)
// Effect 2 (144-150): fires onAuthSuccess() when isRegistered && a PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY flag is set in sessionStorage
```
If a customer starts a social (Apple/Google) sign-in attempt (which sets `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY = true` in sessionStorage per lines 219-222/241-243) and that attempt fails or is abandoned — the flag is never cleared, because clearing only happens inside Effect 2, gated on `isRegistered` — and the customer *then* completes login via the in-app email/OTP flow instead (a realistic retry path), **both effects fire in the same commit**: Effect 1 fires because the drawer/OTP modal is open, and Effect 2 *also* fires because the stale flag is still set. Result: `onAuthSuccess` — which drives the actual wishlist add/navigate action — runs twice for one login event.

I did not just cite a pre-existing test file's output. I wrote my own fixture from scratch (reusing only the PR's already-established `vi.mock` scaffold from `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx`), ran it, and got:
```
MARCEL PROBE RESULT — onAuthSuccess call count: 2
MARCEL PROBE RESULT — clearSessionJSONItem call count: 1
```
then deleted the probe file (`git status --short overrides/app/hooks/` confirmed clean afterward — no residue left in the worktree). None of the PR's existing tests exercise this combination: the "auto-close effect" test never sets `getSessionJSONItem` to return a value, and the "pending intent restoration" tests never open the drawer/OTP modal — each of the two effects is tested in isolation, never together. 🔴 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF (specific to this hook's two-effect design, though the general "two independent effects with overlapping-but-not-exclusive guards" shape is worth watching for elsewhere).
